source_text:
Fragmentum in epistulam ad Philemonem (in catenis)
Phm
1,1 Ἐν πολλαῖς ἐπιστολαῖς ξένον τίθησι ῥῆμα τοῦ μέλλοντος εἰσάγεσθαι λόγου
κατασκευαστικόν, καὶ νῦν ἐπειδὴ ἔμελλεν ἀξιοῦν ὑπὲρ Ὀνησίμου τῇ ἑαυτοῦ ἀξίᾳ–
ἀξία δὲ αὐτοῦ τὸ δεδέσθαι–, τὸ ἀξιόπιστον τῆς παρακλήσεως δείκνυσιν.
thought_title: Paul's unusual word prepares his appeal
orientation: Photius is explaining how Paul opens his letter to Philemon by first establishing his own standing, which is being in chains, so that his appeal for Onesimus will be credible.
pass_a_gloss: In many letters he places an unusual word as preparation for the argument that is about to be introduced, and now, since he was about to make a request on behalf of Onesimus by his own standing—and his standing is being in chains—he shows the credibility of the appeal.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'unusual word' for this fixed term, avoiding 'strange' or 'foreign' which would misrepresent the sense of a striking but not alien expression.
The glossary requires 'preparatory' for this term, capturing that the word serves to establish the ground for the coming argument.
The glossary requires 'standing' for Paul's worth or position, avoiding 'dignity' or 'merit' which carry different connotations.
The glossary requires 'being in chains' for Paul's imprisonment, preserving the literal force of the perfect passive infinitive.
The glossary requires 'credibility' for the trustworthiness of the appeal, avoiding 'reliability' or 'believability'.
The glossary requires 'appeal' for Paul's request on behalf of Onesimus, avoiding 'exhortation' or 'encouragement' which would misread the context.

bible_refs.note: The fragment comments on Philemon 1:1, where Paul opens with his self-designation as a prisoner, which Photius identifies as the unusual word that prepares the appeal.

pass_b_english: In many letters Paul places an unusual word as preparation for the argument he is about to introduce. Here too, since he was about to make a request on behalf of Onesimus, he does so on the basis of his own standing—and his standing is being in chains. In this way he shows the credibility of his appeal.

last_rejected.fix: In many letters Paul places an unusual word preparatory to the argument he is about to introduce.
last_rejected.ruling: κατασκευαστικόν means 'preparatory'; 'as preparation for' conveys same meaning, not a glossary-breaking error.
